replace.vision.segment:
Propose a small mask set from several independent points on one public image.
Use when: comparing plausible regions around the intended object; give 1–8 source-pixel points, usually 3–5 separated interior points. Every point is queried independently, not jointly as one mask prompt, and every point comes back with its own answer.
Effect: world-read-only; binds one current or saved same-round RGB-D view, reuses its image encoding, keeps each point's own SAM alternatives and records immutable masks and per-point query outcomes.
Returns: candidates[] and queries[], one query entry per input point in input order. max_candidates is a PER-POINT budget (default 3, maximum 3): every point's leading mask is admitted before any point's second, so a point that produced a usable mask always keeps one. Each candidate carries its T-index, delivery position, target_ref, score, source queries, geometry and depth/normalization limitations; a mask several points share costs one artifact and is listed under each of them. At most 12 distinct masks and 5 enlarged crops are delivered, and each point reports omitted_over_point_limit and omitted_over_call_cap separately from status no_candidate, which means no mask at that pixel rather than a spent budget. Inspect the proposals and select the intended semantic region.
Does not: require position 0 to be the intended object, prove identity, add sensor resolution by enlargement, mutate the world or grant motion permission. Score orders proposals within one point only; scores from different points are not evidence of which point is right. A point on background, boundary or shadow can return the table, robot or a neighbour. Historical pixels never become current geometry after motion.
On error: correct the named input or source. If no candidate matches the intended region, choose better interior points or another public view; a failed or empty point preserves every other point's results. A disconnected mask keeps the prompted component and reports what was removed.
